title: Local terms
statement:
Use the base $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, finite coefficient ring $A$ and geometric schemes of [sk-d-setup], and the operations of [sk-d-six] on the ordinary pro-etale derived categories. Proper morphisms and open and closed immersions have the meanings of [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-open-immersion] and [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the canonical ordinary adjunction $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and the extension-by-zero adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ of [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions], whose counit is the termwise sheaf counit specified in [def-weil-open-closed-recollement]. Here $j_!$ is extension by zero of [def-weil-extension-by-zero], exact by [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. Dualizing complexes and integrations are those of [def-trf-dualizing-complex], [def-trf-integration] and [sk-d-integral]; all exceptional adjunctions used for them are the constructible ones specified by [def-trf-admissibility], not unrestricted ambient exceptional adjoints.

Let $E$ be proper over $s$, let $\alpha:A_E\to\omega_E$ be a Borel–Moore section, and let $j_B:B\hookrightarrow E$ be an open immersion with closed image. Thus $B$ is also a closed subscheme of $E$ and is proper over $s$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The clopen piece $B$ cuts out the endomorphism

$$
e_B:A_E\xrightarrow{\eta_{j_B}}Rj_{B*}j_B^*A_E\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j_{B!}j_B^*A_E\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{j_B}}A_E,
$$

the unit of $j_B^*\dashv Rj_{B*}$ followed by the counit of $j_{B!}\dashv j_B^*$. The middle arrow is the canonical proper comparison for the clopen immersion, as in [prop-functor-package], clause (3), with $Rj_{B!}=j_{B!}$ for the open immersion. This is the clopen idempotent: $e_B^2=e_B$ by [lem-trf-local-term-clopen-idempotent], clause (1).

Define the local term of $\alpha$ along $B$ by

$$
\operatorname{LT}_B(\alpha):=\int_E(\alpha\circ e_B)\in A.
$$

Writing $\alpha|_B$ for the restricted section of [def-trf-local-term], namely

$$
A_B\simeq j_B^*A_E\xrightarrow{j_B^*\alpha}j_B^*\omega_E\simeq\omega_B,
$$

where the last identification is open purity and dualizing composition as in that definition, this is equivalently

$$
\operatorname{LT}_B(\alpha)=\int_B\alpha|_B.
$$

The equality is [lem-trf-local-term-clopen-idempotent], clause (3). Thus it agrees with the local-term definition of [def-trf-local-term] when the ambient support is proper.

For an opposite pair $(C,c,u),(D,d,v)$ of [sk-d-corr], with pairing of [sk-d-pairing] and $E=E(C,D)$ proper over $s$, put
$$
\operatorname{LT}_B(u,v):=\operatorname{LT}_B(\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}).
$$
This is the proper-ambient case of [def-trf-local-term-pair]. For an endocorrespondence with $\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ proper over $s$ and $B\subseteq\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ clopen, use its trace class of [sk-d-trace-class] to set
$$
\operatorname{LT}_B(u):=\operatorname{LT}_B(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u));
$$
it equals $\operatorname{LT}_B(u,1_K)$ because $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\langle u,1_K\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$ by [lem-trf-trace-class-diagonal-pairing]. At a Frobenius fixed point, $\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}$ means the local term on its reduced clopen point component, as in [def-trf-local-term].
